library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Lindemalm_2005_cladribine"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Lindemalm_2005_cladribine"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2210-5-4> (open access, PMC1079880)

Lindemalm 2005 is a retrospective NONMEM (FOCE with interaction) analysis of
cladribine plasma concentrations pooled from five earlier Swedish and British
PK studies in which the drug was given as a 2-hour or continuous intravenous
infusion, as an oral solution, or as a subcutaneous injection. One integrated
model fits all three routes. The later multiple-sclerosis model of the same
drug, `Savic_2017_cladribine`, is a separate analysis of a different
population and dataset.

# Population

The final analysis used 1102 plasma concentrations from 168 courses in 161
patients (Lindemalm 2005 Methods, Patients). Table 1 of the paper describes
the 163 patients initially included: 129 men and 34 women, mean age 60 years
(range 22-89), mean weight 76 kg (48-118), mean height 174 cm (152-198) and
mean body surface area 1.9 m^2 (1.5-2.4). Diagnoses were hairy cell leukaemia
(84), chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (63), non-Hodgkin lymphoma (7), chronic
myeloid leukaemia (4), acute myeloid leukaemia (3) and Langerhans cell
histiocytosis (2). Mean Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance was 81 mL/min
(Table 2); no patient had severe renal or hepatic impairment.

Doses (Methods, Drug administration) were 5 mg/m^2 (or 0.12 mg/kg) as a 2-hour
IV infusion, 10 mg/m^2 (or 0.24 mg/kg) as an oral solution after an overnight
fast, and 5 mg/m^2 subcutaneously into the abdominal wall. Six patients
received a continuous IV infusion of 4.0-5.6 mg/m^2/24 h for 4-7 days. The
infusion data came from 93 doses, the subcutaneous data from 83 doses and the
oral data from 24 doses; seven patients contributed both IV and oral data.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Lindemalm_2005_cladribine")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every value below is from Lindemalm 2005 Table 3 unless stated otherwise.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL) | 39.3 L/h | Table 3 (RSE 4.9%) |
| `lvc` (V1) | 71.7 L | Table 3 (RSE 13%) |
| `lq` (Q2) | 51.1 L/h | Table 3 (RSE 6.8%) |
| `lvp` (V2) | 475 L | Table 3 (RSE 1.8%) |
| `lq2` (Q3) | 105 L/h | Table 3 (RSE 21%) |
| `lvp2` (V3) | 73.6 L | Table 3 (RSE 13%) |
| `lka_oral` | 1.31 1/h | Table 3 'Oral Ka'; Results |
| `lfdepot_oral` | 0.353 | Table 3 'Oral F'; Results |
| `lka_sc` | 2.48 1/h | Table 3 'Subcutaneous Ka'; Results |
| `lfdepot_sc` | 1 (fixed) | Results: subcutaneous F 'was fixed to this value' |
| `etalcl` | 54% CV | Table 3 IIV |
| `etalvc` | 34% CV | Table 3 IIV |
| `etalq` (shared by Q2, Q3, V3) | 61% CV | Table 3 IIV, identical for Q2, Q3 and V3 |
| `etalvp` | 70% CV | Table 3 IIV |
| `etalka_oral` | 75% CV | Table 3 IIV |
| `etalfdepot_oral` | 4.1% CV | Table 3 IIV; Results ('4 %') |
| `propSdIv` / `propSdOral` / `propSdSc` | 0.191 / 0.232 / 0.162 | Table 3 residual error, footnote 2 |
| `etapropSd` | 24% CV | Table 3 'IIV' of residual error, footnote 3 |
| Three-compartment disposition, first-order absorption without lag | n/a | Results; Methods, Structural pharmacokinetic model |
| Exponential IIV | n/a | Methods, Statistical model |
| Route-specific proportional residual error with IIV on its magnitude | n/a | Methods, Statistical model (Karlsson 1995 method, ref 19) |
| `Cc` in nmol/L | n/a | Methods (assay LOQ 1 nM); Figures 1-3 axes |

# Typical-value checks against the reported half-lives

The paper reports the half-lives of the three disposition phases (0.2, 1.3 and
16 h; Results) and the share of the IV AUC carried by each phase (11%, 24% and
65%; Discussion). Both follow from the Table 3 typical parameters alone, so they
are checked exactly from the model's `ini()` values.

```{r eigen}
mod <- readModelDb("Lindemalm_2005_cladribine")
th <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta
cl <- exp(th[["lcl"]])
vc <- exp(th[["lvc"]])
q <- exp(th[["lq"]])
vp <- exp(th[["lvp"]])
q2 <- exp(th[["lq2"]])
vp2 <- exp(th[["lvp2"]])

kmat <- matrix(
  c(
    -(cl + q + q2) / vc, q / vp, q2 / vp2,
    q / vc, -q / vp, 0,
    q2 / vc, 0, -q2 / vp2
  ),
  nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE
)
ev <- eigen(kmat)
lambda <- -ev$values
# Coefficients of a unit IV bolus into central (amount scale), then the AUC
# carried by each exponential phase.
coef <- ev$vectors[1, ] * solve(ev$vectors, c(1, 0, 0))
auc_share <- (coef / lambda) / sum(coef / lambda)
ord <- order(lambda, decreasing = TRUE)

phase_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  Phase = c("First distribution", "Second distribution", "Terminal"),
  `t1/2 model (h)` = signif(log(2) / lambda[ord], 3),
  `t1/2 paper (h)` = c(0.2, 1.3, 16),
  `AUC share model (%)` = round(100 * auc_share[ord], 1),
  `AUC share paper (%)` = c(11, 24, 65)
)
knitr::kable(phase_tab, caption = "Disposition phases of the typical patient (Lindemalm 2005 Results and Discussion).")

# Deterministic: the reported half-lives are rounded to the digits shown and the
# AUC shares to whole percent.
stopifnot(
  abs(log(2) / lambda[ord][1] - 0.2) < 0.05,
  abs(log(2) / lambda[ord][2] - 1.3) < 0.05,
  abs(log(2) / lambda[ord][3] - 16) < 0.5,
  all(abs(100 * auc_share[ord] - c(11, 24, 65)) < 1.5)
)
```

# Virtual cohort

Original observed data are not publicly available. Each virtual patient draws a
body surface area from a normal distribution with the Table 1 mean and SD
(1.9 +/- 0.2 m^2), truncated to the reported 1.5-2.4 m^2 range, and receives the
per-m^2 dose of their arm. Three single-dose arms of 200 patients each are
simulated (2-hour IV infusion 5 mg/m^2, oral solution 10 mg/m^2, SC injection
5 mg/m^2), sampled densely through 168 h so a terminal half-life and an AUC to
infinity can be estimated for each patient.

`ROUTE_ORAL` and `ROUTE_IV` are set on every row from the arm's route; the model
reads them only to pick the route-specific residual error.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(1079880)
set.seed(1079880)

obs_times <- c(
  0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.25, 2.5, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24,
  30, 36, 48, 60, 72, 96, 120, 144, 168
)

make_arm <- function(n, arm, dose_per_m2, id_offset) {
  bsa <- pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, 1.9, 0.2), 1.5), 2.4)
  cmt_dose <- switch(arm,
    IV = "central",
    Oral = "depot_oral",
    SC = "depot_sc"
  )
  subj <- tibble::tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    arm = arm,
    BSA = bsa,
    ROUTE_ORAL = as.integer(arm == "Oral"),
    ROUTE_IV = as.integer(arm == "IV")
  )
  dose <- subj |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      time = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = cmt_dose, amt = dose_per_m2 * BSA,
      rate = dplyr::if_else(arm == "IV", amt / 2, 0)
    )
  obs <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = 0, rate = 0)
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_arm(200, "IV", 5, id_offset = 0L),
  make_arm(200, "Oral", 10, id_offset = 200L),
  make_arm(200, "SC", 5, id_offset = 400L)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("arm", "BSA")) |>
  as.data.frame()

mod_typical <- mod |> rxode2::zeroRe()
events_typical <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(id %in% c(1L, 201L, 401L)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    amt = dplyr::if_else(evid == 1L, dplyr::if_else(arm == "Oral", 10, 5) * 1.9, 0),
    rate = dplyr::if_else(evid == 1L & arm == "IV", amt / 2, 0)
  )
sim_typical <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typical,
  events = events_typical, keep = c("arm"),
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12
) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 1: concentration-time profiles by route

Figure 1 of the paper pools the observed concentrations of all three routes on
a natural-log axis (log nmol/L from about 0 to 6 over the first 100 h). The
simulated 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles per route are drawn on the same axis.

```{r figure-1}
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% obs_times[obs_times > 0 & obs_times <= 100]) |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05),
    Q50 = quantile(Cc, 0.50),
    Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, log(Q50))) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = log(Q05), ymax = log(Q95), fill = arm), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = arm)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.5, 6.5)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Log (concentration) (nmol/L)",
    colour = "Route", fill = "Route",
    title = "Simulated cladribine profiles, median and 90% interval",
    caption = "Compare with Figure 1 of Lindemalm 2005 (single doses: 2-h IV 5 mg/m^2, oral 10 mg/m^2, SC 5 mg/m^2)."
  )
```

The simulated peaks after the 2-hour infusion and the SC injection sit at
about log 4.5-5.5 and the 24-hour concentrations at about log 1-3, which is the
band the observed points occupy in Figure 1.

## Figure 2: continuous intravenous infusion

Figure 2 shows the observations from repeated and continuous IV
administration; the plateau points between roughly 50 and 170 h lie between
about log 3 and log 4.5 nmol/L. For the typical patient a continuous infusion of
5 mg/m^2/24 h at 1.9 m^2 gives the steady state `R0 / CL`.

```{r figure-2}
r0 <- 5 * 1.9 / 24 # mg/h
ev_inf <- rxode2::et(amt = 5 * 1.9 * 7, rate = r0, cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 200, by = 1)) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(ROUTE_ORAL = 0L, ROUTE_IV = 1L)
sim_inf <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, events = ev_inf, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12) |>
  as.data.frame()

css_expected <- r0 / cl * 1e6 / 285.69 # nmol/L
css_sim <- sim_inf$Cc[sim_inf$time == 160]

ggplot(sim_inf, aes(time, log(Cc))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(3, 4.5), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after start of infusion (h)", y = "Log (concentration) (nmol/L)",
    title = "Typical patient, 7-day continuous infusion of 5 mg/m^2/24 h",
    caption = "Dashed lines: plateau band of the observations in Figure 2 of Lindemalm 2005."
  )

# Deterministic: after 160 h (10 terminal half-lives) the solve is at
# R0/CL; the plateau lies inside the band read from Figure 2.
stopifnot(
  abs(css_sim / css_expected - 1) < 0.01,
  log(css_expected) > 3, log(css_expected) < 4.5
)
c(css_nmol_L = css_expected, log_css = log(css_expected))
```

# PKNCA validation

Clearance and bioavailability are the quantities the paper reports for each
route. PKNCA estimates the AUC to infinity and the terminal half-life per
patient; clearance (or CL/F) is the dose in nmol divided by the AUC.

```{r pknca}
# Integrator undershoot below zero is noise of order atol; assert that, then
# floor it so PKNCA does not take the log of a negative value.
stopifnot(all(sim$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(sim$Cc, na.rm = TRUE), na.rm = TRUE))
conc <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, arm)
dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, arm)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | arm + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | arm + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 0),
  end = c(Inf, 24),
  cmax = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  tmax = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  aucinf.obs = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  half.life = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  auclast = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "half.life", "auclast", "cmax")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(PPTESTCD = dplyr::if_else(PPTESTCD == "auclast", "auc24", PPTESTCD)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, arm, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dose_df |> dplyr::select(id, amt), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    # CL (IV) or CL/F (oral, SC) in L/h: dose in nmol over AUC in nmol*h/L.
    cl.obs = amt * 1e6 / 285.69 / aucinf.obs,
    # Accumulation index for once-daily dosing: AUC over a steady-state
    # dosing interval / AUC over the first interval = AUCinf / AUC0-24.
    accum = aucinf.obs / auc24
  )
```

## Comparison against published values

The reference values are the final-model CL (39.3 L/h) for the IV arm, the
apparent oral clearance from the paper's route-specific supplementary fit
(105 L/h; Results), the final-model CL / F for the SC arm (39.3 L/h with F
fixed at 1), and the 16-hour terminal half-life (Results). `ncaComparisonTable()`
reports the median across patients.

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm, ~cl.obs, ~half.life,
  "IV", 39.3, 16,
  "Oral", 105, 16,
  "SC", 39.3, 16
)
sim_long <- nca_wide |>
  dplyr::select(arm, cl.obs, half.life) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(cl.obs, half.life), names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "PPORRES")

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_long,
  reference = published,
  by = "arm",
  units = c(cl.obs = "L/h", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated (median) vs. published clearance and terminal half-life. * differs from reference by >20%.")
```

The median clearance of a cohort with 54% CV IIV on CL sits close to the typical
value because clearance is log-normal, and the oral CL/F matches the paper's
separately estimated 105 L/h (39.3 / 0.353 = 111 L/h in the final model). The
PKNCA half-life is fitted to each patient's terminal points within 168 h and is
the median across patients, so it carries the IIV of every disposition
parameter on top of the typical 16 h.

```{r nca-checks}
med <- nca_wide |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    cl = median(cl.obs), thalf = median(half.life, na.rm = TRUE),
    accum_q10 = quantile(accum, 0.1, na.rm = TRUE),
    accum_q50 = median(accum, na.rm = TRUE),
    accum_q90 = quantile(accum, 0.9, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(med, digits = 2, caption = "Per-arm medians and accumulation-index quantiles.")

# Typical-value bioavailability: dose-normalised AUC ratio against the IV arm.
auc_typ <- sim_typical |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    auc = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
f_oral_typ <- (auc_typ$auc[auc_typ$arm == "Oral"] / 19) / (auc_typ$auc[auc_typ$arm == "IV"] / 9.5)
f_oral_typ

stopifnot(
  # Structural: a mis-transcribed CL, F or unit moves these medians by tens
  # of percent. Bands are wide enough for cohort-to-cohort variation of the
  # median of 200 log-normal draws (SE ~4%).
  abs(med$cl[med$arm == "IV"] / 39.3 - 1) < 0.15,
  abs(med$cl[med$arm == "Oral"] / (39.3 / 0.353) - 1) < 0.15,
  abs(med$cl[med$arm == "SC"] / 39.3 - 1) < 0.15,
  # Trapezoidal typical-value F over a 168-h grid: within 5% of 0.353.
  abs(f_oral_typ / 0.353 - 1) < 0.05
)
```

## Accumulation index

The paper reports an accumulation index between 1.02 and 3.05 for repeated IV
dosing (the extremes, for the patients with the shortest and longest terminal
half-lives of 5 and 58 h; Results). In the simulated IV arm the index is
`AUCinf / AUC0-24` after a single infusion, which equals the steady-state to
first-interval AUC ratio for once-daily dosing.

```{r accumulation}
iv_acc <- nca_wide |> dplyr::filter(arm == "IV")
ggplot(iv_acc, aes(half.life, accum)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  annotate("point", x = c(5, 58), y = c(1.02, 3.05), colour = "red", size = 3) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Terminal half-life (h, PKNCA)", y = "Accumulation index",
    title = "Accumulation index vs. terminal half-life, simulated IV arm",
    caption = "Red points: the extremes reported by Lindemalm 2005 (Results)."
  )

# The reported range spans 161 patients; the central 80% of the simulated
# cohort must lie inside it.
stopifnot(
  med$accum_q10[med$arm == "IV"] > 1.02,
  med$accum_q90[med$arm == "IV"] < 3.05
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Shared eta on Q2, Q3 and V3.** Table 3 reports the same IIV (61%) with the
  same RSE (17%) for Q2, Q3 and V3. The maintainers read this as one random
  effect shared by the three parameters (one NONMEM ETA), which reproduces the
  reported marginal CV of each. Three independent random effects constrained to
  one variance (`$OMEGA BLOCK(1) SAME`) would give the same marginal CVs but no
  correlation between them; the paper does not say which was used.
- **CV to variance.** Table 3 gives IIV as a coefficient of variation; the
  log-normal variances are `log(1 + CV^2)`.
- **Residual error scale.** The Table 3 residual-error values (0.191, 0.232,
  0.162) are read as proportional standard deviations (fractions), consistent
  with the table's other variability terms being on the CV scale. The 24% IIV in
  residual variability is an exponential random effect on that SD
  (`propSd * exp(etapropSd)`), the implementation of the cited method (Karlsson
  1995).
- **Molar mass.** Concentrations are returned in nmol/L, the unit of the assay
  and of every figure in the paper, using the cladribine molar mass of
  285.69 g/mol, which is not stated in the paper.
- **No covariates.** None of the screened covariates (sex, age, weight, height,
  BSA, creatinine clearance, liver tests, lymphocyte count, diagnosis) was
  retained, so the virtual cohort varies only BSA, and only to set the per-m^2
  dose.
- **Single-dose design.** The paper's courses were mostly once-daily infusions
  or injections over several days; the cohort here gives single doses so each
  route's profile and NCA can be compared directly. The accumulation index is
  derived from the single-dose IV profile.
- **Errata.** No correction notice for this article was found in Europe PMC
  (checked 2026-10-29).
